profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting in an ML research lab evaluating the near-final experiment package for a paper titled "Deep Learning Architectures for FSCV, a Comparison." The comparison already includes InceptionTime, a naive multilayer perceptron, and several other DNN baselines trained on labeled in vitro FSCV recordings from carbon fiber electrodes, and the team now needs to decide whether the current design can be locked for the final cluster rerun and manuscript tables. The agenda is to review whether the design really supports the paper's three reviewer-visible claims: performance in the out-of-probe setting, sensitivity to artificially induced electrical noise, and the ability to predict when a model will be errant for a given probe. The expected outcome is a decision on whether the package is 'camera-ready for rerun' with only minor edits, or whether specific structural changes to splits, stress tests, or reporting artifacts are still needed before sign-off.

members.name: Dr. Maya Srinivasan
members.expertise: Machine learning for electrochemical sensing, experimental validation strategy, and reviewer-facing scientific framing
members.background: Maya leads a neurochemical sensing lab that has previously published FSCV prediction work with classical models and smaller deep-learning baselines; she usually reviews projects at the level of whether the evidence package, figures, and wording will survive skeptical peer review.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the paper moving, but only if the final tables and manuscript claims cannot be interpreted as overstating generalization or robustness; she is especially wary of subtle leakage or overly narrow stress tests that would only surface during review.
hidden_assumptions: When the paper says 'out-of-probe,' every voltammogram from a physical carbon fiber electrode must be excluded from both model fitting and all threshold-setting for that probe's evaluation.
A 'noise robustness' result should characterize behavior across a realistic range of injected electrical noise amplitudes, not just confirm a ranking under one synthetic condition.
If the paper claims the model can predict when it will be errant for a given probe, the error-flagging threshold should be fixed without using outputs from that same probe family or session type.

When she asks whether the package is 'ready to lock,' she means the exact reviewer-facing artifacts for the Results section—split definition, final table schema, and figure captions—are settled enough that the manuscript text can be written around them without later reinterpretation.

members.name: Ethan Cole
members.expertise: Deep learning experimentation, time-series benchmark pipelines, reproducible training infrastructure, and result packaging
members.background: Ethan built the comparison codebase, standardized preprocessing for the FSCV corpus, and produced the existing architecture sweep; he tends to reason in terms of fold definitions, cached artifacts, and what can be rerun reproducibly on the cluster with minimal pipeline changes.
members.private_state: He wants the meeting to end with permission to freeze the current benchmark structure, because changing split semantics or expanding the stress-test protocol would invalidate cached runs and delay submission by at least another compute cycle.
hidden_assumptions: In this benchmark, 'out-of-probe' is adequately represented by the existing held-out acquisition-group split, because each acquisition group is effectively tied to one probe setup and therefore operationally close to unseen-probe evaluation.
A 'noise robustness' section is sufficient if the common injected-noise condition at the lab's standard amplitude shows the relative ranking and degradation pattern among architectures.

Showing when a model will be errant for a given probe can rely on a global confidence or residual-thresholding rule tuned once on pooled validation outputs, as long as the final test fold is untouched.

When he hears 'ready to lock,' he interprets it as meaning the experiment manifest for the final cluster rerun is frozen—config files, split IDs, and table-generation scripts are not expected to change structurally afterward.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss whether the current design properly evaluates the 'out-of-probe' case.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means strict leave-entire-electrode-out evaluation: all scans from a physical carbon fiber electrode are absent from training, validation, and any threshold tuning when that probe is tested.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the existing held-out acquisition-group split, where the test fold corresponds to a distinct recording group that is usually associated with one probe setup, even if other scans from the same underlying electrode or preparation lineage may appear elsewhere in the pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to the lab shorthand 'out-of-probe,' and because acquisition groups are often probe-specific in practice, the looser operational meaning sounds close enough that neither expects the term itself needs unpacking.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the noise robustness check
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the paper needs a 'noise robustness' or 'noise response' result before sign-off.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes robustness means showing how predictive error and model ranking behave across multiple injected electrical noise amplitudes, such as a sweep from low to severe perturbation, so reviewers can judge whether the observed stability is structural.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes robustness is adequately demonstrated by the single standard artificial noise setting already used in the draft figures, because the paper's claim is comparative and not a full stress-test characterization.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Neither questions that a noise experiment exists, and both can point to the same draft plot as 'the noise result'; the mismatch lies only in the unspoken evidentiary bar for what that plot is supposed to establish.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to evaluating whether the model can 'predict when it will be errant for a given probe.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes near-deployment behavior in scope: the error-flagging method should be evaluated as something applied after encountering a new probe, with thresholds fixed independently of that probe's own outputs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 treats it as a benchmark-side auxiliary analysis: any confidence or residual-based signal that identifies likely bad predictions on held-out examples is in scope, even if the threshold was tuned globally on pooled validation data spanning many probes and sessions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'for a given probe' sounds concrete and shared, but one hears it as a deployment context while the other hears it simply as the unit on which examples are grouped for reporting, so the gap hides behind natural benchmark language.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to 'lock the package'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss whether the experiment package is 'ready to lock' before the final rerun.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes 'lock' means the reviewer-facing Results artifacts are frozen: the exact split definition behind Table 1, the schema of the robustness table, and the captions/wording that will anchor manuscript claims should no longer need conceptual revision after the rerun.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes 'lock' means the technical rerun manifest is frozen: config YAMLs, split IDs already serialized in the dataloader, and the table-generation script can be sent to the cluster unchanged, with any remaining claim-narrowing handled later in manuscript text.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use 'lock' as routine project shorthand and are focused on moving the paper forward; because the phrase naturally fits both artifact-freezing and interpretation-freezing, the disagreement survives as a silent presupposition rather than an explicit dispute.

turns.inner_thought: I need to determine whether the reviewer-facing Results package is actually settled, not just whether Ethan can rerun the code. If we say out-of-probe, I mean strict leave-entire-electrode-out with no contamination through validation or threshold setting. If we say noise robustness, I need more than a token perturbation result. And if we claim the model can predict when it will be errant for a given probe, that has to read like something that would hold on a genuinely new probe, not just an internal benchmark trick. I don't want to stall the paper, but I also don't want a review cycle derailed by avoidable ambiguity.
